newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening lower in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening lower in thin trading.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open lower in quiet trading on Monday, continuing the trend of Friday afternoon, when a fast and furious sell-off slashed gains.
The Dow Industrials eked out a rise of just over ten points to close at 6,484.40 after slashing earlier strong gains. For the week, it rose 179.53 points.
"Friday's triple-witching left something of a bitter taste," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
"Triple-witching" is the simultaneous expiration of stock options, index options and futures.
The Standard & Poor's March index of futures was off 1.25 to 756. The long bond was up 2/32 to yield 6.60 percent.
Wall Street analysts said they expected very quiet trading due to the Christmas holiday on Wednesday.
